Recap / Answers (high level):

- Logs: by default we retain request/exec logs for 365 days. We can discuss shorter log retention windows for PII-sensitive customers and can offer contractual limits (e.g., 90 days) subject to technical feasibility and pricing impact.

Jordan — quick clarifications from our security/compliance team on the deletion/backups/logs items you raised: 

- Primary data deletion: upon a verified deletion request (guide: authenticated account owner + ticket), we remove customer-controlled objects from active storage within 30 days and provide a deletion confirmation. This covers model inputs/outputs and customer-uploaded artifacts.
- Backups: snapshots are maintained for disaster recovery. Standard snapshot retention is 90 days. Snapshots are immutable while in the retention window; we can include contractual language for an expedited purge (target window 30–90 days depending on the storage tier) but need to set expectations that cross-region replication and cold-storage lifecycle jobs can affect timing.
- Log retention: default 365 days. We retain access logs (who/when), request metadata (timestamp, model, token counts), and system-level exec traces (aggregated). We can implement a shortened retention for logs containing PII-heavy fields, but full deletion from all analytic/monitoring tiers can require coordination (we recommend 90 days as a common contractable compromise).

Notes on GDPR/HIPAA:
- For GDPR: we support data subject requests and can map our deletion flows to customer DSAR processes; we provide evidence of deletion upon request.
- For HIPAA: we support BAAs and have controls in place; we will need to confirm specific PHI handling patterns in your implementation to ensure scope.

If you share the vendor questionnaire (or point us to the sections you care about), I can route to the right SME and aim to return answers in ~2 business days.

—Neha Kapoor
